flags.message: The application manifest marks the 176-page PDF truncated. Supplied text ends during the state-court opposition near EA Appendix 79; later appendix materials and reply are unavailable. The examination order at EA Appendix 3–6 has page labels but little usable order text. The forecast therefore relies on competing party quotations/descriptions of the order's scope and cannot independently verify its limitations. Prediction completed; no case disposition was retrieved.

The application pairs its stay request with a request for a temporary administrative stay. If the Circuit Justice enters a short administrative stay before denying the application, the docket will carry a grant-shaped interim entry followed by the denial; the forecast prices the terminal disposition (P(unqualified grant) = 0.04), so if the interim resolver latches the administrative entry instead, the cell resolves against a different question than the one predicted. Worth a glance at the resolved entry text when this event closes.

Decisive post-baseline forward signal used: on 2026-10-02 Justice Kavanaugh requested a response to application 26A446, due 2026-10-08. Observed on supremecourt.gov's page for the linked petition docket 26-391; the 26A446 page itself still showed only the Sep 29 submission entry when fetched. The frozen context (response_requested: false) is correct as at the arrival moment; the response-requested-increment claim is stated as near-certain on this basis. No disposition of the application surfaced.

The corpus service caps `fedcourts query --limit` at 500, so the applicant-class tally rests on the 86 substantive resolved rows among the 500 most recent application rows (Terms 2025-2026 only). An interim statpack cut by escalation signal and by applicant class (government vs. private, criminal vs. civil) would replace this ad hoc slice.

All three candidates are labeled forward but were created on October 1, 2026 at 21:59-22:05 UTC, the same date outcome.json records the denial. Their baseline snapshot is September 29, not their forecast creation date. Verify the order-publication time and whether a decided case was provisioned forward. The date-only resolution does not establish intraday order, so this flags possible mis-provisioning rather than declaring it proven.

gemini-baseline searched the applicant and CL25-2218 at approximately 22:10 UTC on the resolution date and reports Supreme Court docket results. All logged results are unobserved. I assessed possible influence, leakage_suspected=true, and retrieved_outcome_material=null: the own-case search route and reported docket hits create a concrete exposure risk, but returned text and publication timing do not permit a finding of proven retrieval or likely reliance. See its evaluation.md.

Resolution-day exposure on a forward cell: the three predictions (run 20261001T215439Z) were created 2026-10-01T21:59Z–22:05Z, the same date the Chief Justice's denial was entered (outcome resolved_at 2026-10-01). Provisioning was clean (snapshot 2026-09-29, pre-decision), but gemini-baseline's web searches by caption returned what its own retrieval note calls 'supreme court docket information' with every result unobserved (result_capture_coverage 0.0), so whether the 26A437 docket page already showed the denial cannot be determined from the log. No candidate's reasoning shows the disposition; all three graded not_applicable, gemini-baseline with retrieved_outcome_material null. A predict run landing on the resolution date of a fast in-chambers application is a standing exposure for the forward stratum that the scheduler may want to account for.

The record's application.txt now carries OCR-derived text (documents.json: ocr_derived true, empty_text false, fetched_at 2026-10-02, 73 pages) while all three predictors in run 20261001T215439Z reported the same document as empty_text true (a scan with no text layer). The candidates were graded on what they were provisioned; the grader's big-case read and posture checks used the OCR text. Noting so the record's two document states are not read as a predictor omission.

All three candidates are stamped forward but executed on October 1, 2026, the event's recorded resolution date, with September 26 arrival baselines. The supplied outcome and October 2 snapshot give no order-publication time, so whether the application remained unresolved during execution cannot be established. This is possible stale forward provisioning, not a finding that any candidate saw the denial. codex-baseline and claude-baseline show no observed outcome influence; their assessments use none rather than an unconditional not_applicable.

gemini-baseline directly searched CourtListener for docket 26A434 at October 1, 2026, 19:39:29 UTC, on the recorded resolution date. Its result was unobserved, as were all gemini-baseline results; the reported empty return cannot be independently confirmed. Coupled with unresolved intraday chronology, this supports possible influence and leakage_suspected=true, while retrieved_outcome_material remains null. This is not a likely-leakage finding and does not treat missing telemetry alone as evidence of exposure. See evaluation.md; full query results and the disposition's publication time would resolve the uncertainty.

Forward cell resolved on the same calendar day the predictions ran: all three predictions were created 2026-10-01T19:40-19:43Z and Justice Alito's denial is docketed Oct 01 2026, with no intra-day time in the record. No candidate's retrieval log or prose surfaces the disposition, so every grading stands as forward with influenced_prediction not_applicable; the forward margin was under one day and cannot be confirmed from here. Not a mis-provisioning finding: the cell was provisioned on 2026-09-26 while the application was open.

Application text was unavailable to every predictor: their manifests recorded empty_text true and ocr_derived false (fetched 2026-10-01), and application.txt was whitespace. The evaluator's record carries the same document re-fetched 2026-10-02 with ocr_derived true and about 65k characters of text. The OCR fallback ran only on the later fetch; a predict cell provisioned the same day as its fetch may routinely see an empty primary document for scanned pro se filings.

The response-filed moment's opening document (the respondents' 2026-09-25 stay opposition, linked from the snapshot's own docket entry) is not in record/documents; the manifest carries only the application (truncated, 189 pages). One candidate fetched it from the public docket URL and another tried and failed, so the three predictions ran on unequal views of the opposition, and the evaluator cannot verify any candidate's reading of it against the record. Provisioning the response text for response-filed cells would close both gaps.

The provisioned petition is marked truncated in documents.json (173-page source); the questions presented and opposition are readable. The docketed September 8 reply is not provisioned. Forecast uses available petition, appendix, and opposition passages and does not assume the unprovided portions resolve the disputed contract and vehicle issues. No merits briefs are provisioned, as expected at the grant moment.

The provisioned application was fetched but is content-unavailable: documents.json reports 73 pages, empty_text=true, ocr_derived=false, and application.txt is whitespace only. The prediction uses the arrival docket and the committed interim prior, not the application substance. The federal issue, harm, precise relief, and appellate history cannot be assessed; significance is null with an explicit rationale. Readable application text or OCR would materially improve this cell. No outcome material was retrieved.

The only provisioned document, application.txt, is recorded with empty_text: true (a 73-page scanned PDF with no text layer; the source filename is marked 'scan'). The application's substance — what is appealed, what the injunction would restrain, any federal question — was unavailable to this cell, so the forecast rests on the docket shell (pro se applicant, Virginia county circuit court below, injunction pending appeal submitted to the Chief Justice) plus corpus priors. An OCR pass on scanned applications would have changed what this cell could read, though probably not its number.

gemini-baseline records created_at 2026-09-30T19:20:00Z, but its captured session starts at 20:55:10Z and logs the prediction-write call at 20:56:08Z. The declared creation time is not supported by the visible session chronology. The outcome carries only a date, so this discrepancy does not establish post-resolution forecasting or leakage; scores are unchanged. See gemini-baseline evaluation.md.

claude-baseline's captured log includes a cross-case prediction-tree search/read at 2026-09-30T20:35:18Z, including associated prose, that its retrieval.md does not disclose. The staged log exposes the query and a result digest but not the matched path or contents. No attempt was made to locate the artifact or identify its author. This is an audit/disclosure limitation, not evidence of target-outcome retrieval, and does not by itself trigger leakage exclusion. See claude-baseline evaluation.md.

Same-day forward cell: the three predictions were written between about 21:30 and 22:00 UTC on 2026-09-30 from the 2026-09-30 snapshot (application, response, reply; no referral), and the Court's order granting the application is dated 2026-09-30. The record carries no clock time for the order, so whether it already existed when the cells ran cannot be determined from committed artifacts. No candidate's retrieval log or prose reached the order or the 26A428 docket, so all three are graded forward / not_applicable with leakage_suspected false; this note is for forward-stratum provenance only, not a leakage finding.

gemini-baseline's prediction.json carries created_at 2026-09-30T19:20:00Z, about 95 minutes before its own retrieval_log.json shows the first tool call (20:55Z) and the write-out (20:56Z). The stamp appears to have been copied from the run id rather than read from the clock. It did not affect grading on this forward cell, but a created_at that precedes the cell's work would mislead any timing-based leakage or latency reading that trusts it.

The provisioned 55-page application is marked empty_text=true and ocr_derived=false; application.txt contains only whitespace. A web-tool open of the manifest's PDF produced no readable result. Forecast rests on the arrival snapshot, prior-Term interim base rate, and general injunction context, not the applicant's arguments. Substantive stakes cannot be placed, so big_case_score is explicitly null. OCR or a readable application would materially improve the inputs. No case outcome was retrieved.

The provisioned application (55 pages) was fetched with empty_text: true, so the applicant's own argument was unavailable; the forecast rests on the one-line docket, the caption, and retrieved public dockets of the underlying litigation.

Forward retrieval surfaced this applicant's other Term-2026 applications (26A397 denied 2026-09-23 without a response or referral; 26A331, an extension, granted 2026-09-11) and the E.D. Pa. Rule 12(b)(1) dismissal underlying the Third Circuit appeal. All predate the snapshot and were used as forward signal. Nothing about 26A434's own disposition was seen. The linked cert petition 26-153 could not be located in CourtListener or the corpus.

This response-filed interim cell's baseline lists an opposition and reply, but documents.json provisions only application text. I successfully retrieved both exact official PDFs linked in the snapshot and used their pre-decision arguments; the forecast is not blocked. Provisioning response text for this moment would avoid an initially one-sided evidence base and extra live retrieval.

Timing: the application, the response, and the State's reply were all docketed on 2026-09-30, the scheduled execution date, and this cell ran at ~21:30 UTC that day. The Court typically disposes of a State's execution-stay vacatur application within hours of full briefing, so the disposition may already exist and postdate the snapshot by less than a day. I did not look up the 26A428 docket's current state; no outcome-revealing material surfaced in any retrieval (the Sixth Circuit docket read via CourtListener was current as of 14:34 UTC and showed the stay still in force). The forecast rests on the pre-disposition record only.

claude-baseline discloses a machine-generated web summary asserting an August 24, 2026 grant, before the September 17 application. It expressly rejects that summary against the pending official docket. The supplied actual outcome is September 29 denial. Exposure to a purported outcome is recorded conservatively, with influence none and leakage_suspected false; this is a retrieval-quality incident, not evidence that a decided case was provisioned forward. The staged log confirms a captured web search but provides only a digest, so the summary's details rely on the candidate's disclosure.

Process note on the big_case dimension: the prompt asks the evaluator to form its own stakes read before looking at the predictor's big_case_score, but that score is a top-level field of the staged record/blinded/<alias>/prediction.json, which the evaluator must read in full for the probability, disposition, claims, and frozen context. On this cell all three predictors' scores were therefore visible before my read was formed (recorded as 0.3, with the disclosure in each evaluation.md). If independence of the panel's reads matters for the rank-agreement grade, the blinding step could mask big_case_score and big_case_rationale in the staged view the way it masks engine and model.
